Q: Oracle SQL Developer, Execute Script won't stop running A:

This might be because of DB lock. Try executing the below query to remove the lock. (Ps: Considering your schema has the privilege)

  1. Get the session id: SELECT SESSION_ID FROM DBA_DML_LOCKS WHERE NAME = <TABLE_NAME>;

  2. With the session id get SID and Serial# SELECT SID, SERIAL# FROM V$SESSION WHERE SID IN ( SELECT SESSION_ID FROM DBA_DML_LOCKS WHERE NAME = <TABLE_NAME> );

  3. Kill the session ALTER SYSTEM KILL SESSION 'SID, SERIAL#';

Q: Spring Boot response has already been committed exception for request to resources A:

I had the same exception in my application deployed as WAR on WildFly server. This app was referred to static files outside the WAR archive and, for an occasional reason, it didn't have rights to read files from the static directory. So, if you have a situation like this, check your file permissions.

Q: Google Maps Free API for NGO project A:

You don't necessarily need Google Maps for this, especially if the project has a very limited budget.

If you only need to convert an event address into latitude/longitude, you can use a geocoding service. For an OpenStreetMap-based solution, Nominatim can be used for small-scale applications. However, the public Nominatim server has strict usage limits and should not be treated as a free unlimited production API. It currently limits heavy use to a maximum of 1 request/second and requires proper attribution.

For displaying the map, you can use a library such as Leaflet with OpenStreetMap-based tiles. Your event record could simply store:

latitude
longitude
address

Then, when the event page is opened, you can place a marker at those coordinates. You don't need to geocode the same address every time someone views the event.

If you prefer Google Maps, it isn't completely free, but Google Maps Platform does provide free monthly usage for individual SKUs. For example, Google's current pricing lists a 10,000-event free monthly cap for Dynamic Maps and Geocoding, although billing-enabled projects and an API key are required.

Another simple option is to store the coordinates and provide a "View on Google Maps" link. That avoids embedding a Google map in your application.

So for a small nonprofit project, I'd recommend:

Address → geocoding service → save lat/lng → display with Leaflet/OpenStreetMap

or, if you want Google's data/features:

Google Maps Platform → enable billing + API key → monitor usage

The important point is that being an NGO does not automatically make Google Maps API usage free. You should choose the service based on expected usage and its current pricing/terms.

Q: How can I create a formula that reads the hierarchy number structure and add the parent code for the child in Google Sheet? A:

This formula will work equally well with numeric values and text strings that look like numbers:

=arrayformula(iferror(let(
  v, to_text(D2:D),
  if(regexmatch(v, "0{6}$"),,
    left(left(v, len(regexreplace(v, "(00)*$",)) - 2) & "000000", 8)
  )
)))

...with pretty good performance.

The iferror() is required to handle blank rows. In the event there aren't any blank rows, as is the case on the sample spreadsheet, you can leave it out to improve performance further.

See let(), regexmatch() and regexreplace().
